text:
PsiQuantum Commits $250,000 to South Chicago Quantum Workforce Development

Students participating in hands-on STEM activities. Source: PsiQuantum

Photonic quantum computing developer PsiQuantum has announced a $250,000 philanthropic investment to expand local STEM education, higher education programs, and career training in South Chicago. As the anchor tenant of the Illinois Quantum and Microelectronics Park (IQMP), the company is funding workforce development initiatives across surrounding communities to build a local talent pipeline for the emerging regional quantum industry.

The funding initiative allocates resources across K-12 education, higher education, and community-based STEM programs:

Higher Education Infrastructure: Direct grants to Chicago State University’s Quantum Education, Science, and Technology Center (CQuEST), STEM Explorations Camp, and Quantum Teacher Training programs, alongside curriculum support at Olive-Harvey College (City Colleges of Chicago) focused on supply chain, data analytics, and quantum technologies.

Secondary School Curriculum Expansion: Funding for George Washington High School and St. Francis De Sales High School to enhance STEM course offerings, upgrade classroom technology, and provide specialized teacher training.

Community STEM Access: Grants to Project SYNCERE and Phalanx Family Services to expand extracurricular STEM learning opportunities for local students.

The workforce investment follows ongoing construction at PsiQuantum’s utility-scale quantum computing site at the IQMP campus since its September 2025 groundbreaking. The company previously provided targeted equipment grants to local schools, including funding virtual reality systems, robotics, and drone technology at Bowen High School. By funding educator certification, higher education research hubs, and vocational pathways alongside its primary hardware fabrication site, PsiQuantum aims to connect South Chicago communities directly to industrial opportunities created by the state’s quantum park ecosystem.
